@neerajnathanyYes!   
  
The notch is just the nicest place for it, not the only one. On a Mac without a notch (or with the lid closed on an external display), Termy skips the notch and moves everything to the menu bar: the icon changes color when an agent needs you, approval notifications have Allow / Deny buttons right on them, and the panel drops down from the menu bar on whichever screen you're using, with the same approval banner. If your MacBook is open next to the monitor, the notch keeps working on the laptop screen.

Share [...] Pro adds the Agent Office, a pixel-art office where every agent and subagent sits at a desk. A raised hand means someone needs you, and the "Done today" whiteboard lists what got finished. New in 1.4.5: chat with any agent from the side panel. Pro also includes Silent mode (agents keep working, nothing pings you), review notes on diffs, git worktree sessions, Termy Browser, on-device Whisper dictation, checkpoints and usage insights.

Pricing: free to use. Pro is $4.99 once, with no subscription and a 14-day free trial. For launch week, code PRODUCTHUNT takes 30% off Pro.

Termy needs macOS 26, and the notch features need a MacBook with a notch (everything else works from the menu bar icon).

I'd love to hear how you run your agents and what you'd want the notch to show next.

Upvote (5) [...] and a terminal drops down. There's a tab for every project open in Xcode, VS Code or Cursor, and Claude Code or Codex starts in the right folder.

- The notch shows working / needs you / done, read from Claude Code's and Codex's own hooks rather than guessed from the screen. When the agent wants to run a command, Allow / Deny appears right in the notch.

- Tabs come back with their conversations after a restart, or after the agent crashes.

- The menu bar card shows every session and your Claude and Codex plan limits.

- Calm, readable themes (Soft Dark, Warm Night, Paper) and readable fonts built in.
